content.text: In Brief Fall 2026 American Association for Cancer Research The American Association for Cancer Research awarded three grants totaling $330,000 to support the research of Temidayo Fadelu, MD, MPH, Srinivas Viswanathan, MD, PhD, and Alice Tzeng, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. These grants advance research in breast and kidney cancer and ALK-positive lung cancer, with the potential to improve care and treatment for patients worldwide. American Heart Association The American Heart Association awarded grants totaling $478,668 to investigators Yu Lei, PhD, and Gerard Pernes, PhD. The funding will support studies of muscle adaptation to exercise in heart failure and itaconate as a regulator of metabolic disease—research that may advance cardiovascular science and inform future cancer therapies. American Society of Hematology The American Society of Hematology awarded $465,000 in total to investigators: Alba Rodriguez-Meira, PhD (2026 Basic/Translational Research Fellow Scholar Award); Cynthia Hahn, MD, PhD (2026 Basic/Translational Research Fellow to Faculty Scholar Award); Benson George, MD, PhD, and Frederick Tsai, MD, PhD (2025 Research Training Awards for Fellows); and Miriam Osei, MD, MPH (2025 Hematology Inclusion Pathway Fellow Award). Seth Brufsky, Adam Brufsky, and Naomi Brufsky Waltman Seth, Adam, and Naomi Brufsky made a $100,000 gift to honor their mother, establishing the Ruth C. Brufsky Fund—a tribute to the Ruth C. Brufsky Memorial Lecture in Medical Ethics. The fund supports emerging leaders in the field, helping shape high-quality, principled cancer care. It will also expand year-round medical ethics research through Dana-Farber's Cancer Ethics Research Initiative, led by Gregory A. Abel, MD, MPH. Cookies for Kids’ Cancer A generous $300,000 grant from Cookies for Kids’ Cancer is supporting Yana Pikman, MD, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute as she conducts research to evaluate the MAT2A protein, with chemotherapy and in combination with other drugs. The results will inform clinical trials for patients with aggressive T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. Pat Chadwick and Norm Cantin Pat Chadwick and Norm Cantin, along with their families, made a gift of $100,000 to the Young and Strong Program, part of the Susan F. Smith Center for Women’s Cancers at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Ann Partridge, MD, MPH, and Kristen Brantley, PhD, will use these funds to research young-onset breast cancer, identify high-risk patients, and improve personalization of care. Deborah Cummings Fall 2026By Christina Tavella Inspired by the exceptional care her 4-year-old grandson Harrison received at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Deborah Cummings has generously arranged for $100,000 from her estate to support cancer research and patient services. Through this gift, Deborah is helping advance innovations that improve outcomes for patients like Harrison. Myron and Laura Dickerman With a generous gift of $100,000 to the Laura P. and Myron J. Dickerman Fund for Endometrial Cancer Research, Joyce F. Liu, MD, MPH, and her team will help advance research focused on treating recurrent ovarian and endometrial cancers. This vital funding will support several promising phase I clinical trials that address a critical gap in early stage cancer research funding. Seth and Melissa Finkelstein Seth and Melissa Finkelstein made a gift to support the research of Toni Choueiri, MD, Mark Pomerantz, MD, and Paul L. Nguyen, MD, MBA, as well as the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Pediatric Resource Program. Their generosity advances pioneering prostate cancer research and helps provide timely financial assistance to pediatric patients and families. Fund for Innovation in Cancer Informatics Fall 2026By Brendan Monahan The Fund for Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded grants totaling $448,000 to support the work of Volker Hovestadt, PhD, Christopher Manz, MD, MSHP, Charlotta Lindvall, MD, PhD, and Alexi A. Wright, MD, MPH, at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Spanning rapid epigenomic classification of acute leukemia and AI-enabled serious illness communication, these projects aim to strengthen patient-centered care and accelerate diagnostic innovation. Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl presented by SharkNinja The 2026 Jimmy Fund Scooper Bowl® presented by SharkNinja took place in Boston’s Seaport over three sunny days in June. Attendees were able to enjoy endless scoops from more than 10 different ice cream brands, and the event raised a record-breaking $565,000 to support cancer care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Juliana Greenfield Family Foundation The Juliana Greenfield Family Foundation together with the Mazzetta Family Foundation made gifts totaling $300,000 to help Robbie Majzner, MD, and his team advance novel clinical trials testing an enhanced CAR T-cell therapy approach for children and young adults with high-risk neuroblastoma who experience recurrence or are unresponsive to treatments. Charles A. King Trust The Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded the 2025–2027 Sara Elizabeth O’Brien Trust Fellowship, totaling $206,000, to Carlos Mendez-Dorantes, PhD. This grant will support his research on repetitive DNA and L1 biology, which may inform future cancer therapies. Judy and Peter Kovler Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received a $100,000 gift from Judy and Peter Blum Kovler Foundation in support of invasive lobular carcinoma research led by Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, bringing their cumulative giving to $550,000. The Kovlers’ generosity helps advance research into this understudied type of breast cancer and supports the development of novel therapies for patients. Yury Labintsev and Ekaterina Labintceva Yury Labintsev and Ekaterina Labintceva recently made a gift to establish the Timon Labintcev Pediatric Brain Tumor Fellowship Award at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in honor of their late son, Timon. Under the direction of Mariella Filbin, MD, PhD, the awarded fellow will help accelerate progress in pediatric neuro-oncology and advance global knowledge of multiple forms of pediatric brain tumors. The Lewin Fund to Fight Women’s Cancers The Lewin Fund to Fight Women’s Cancers made a $300,000 gift to equally support gynecologic cancer research led by Joyce Liu, MD, MPH, and Panos Konstantinopoulos, MD, PhD, the R.J. Corman Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School and Dana-Farber. This investment will help assess how to optimize the use of antibody-drug conjugates for ovarian tumors and advance a clinical trial to validate new treatment approaches for endometrial and ovarian cancers. Mahadevia Family Fund Akshay, Geeta, Aalap, and Pinki Mahadevia’s generous gift of $100,000 establishes the Mahadevia Family Fund at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, under the direction of Sara Tolaney, MD, MPH, chief of the Division of Breast Oncology. The gift will support research on triple negative breast cancer and advance cutting-edge discovery science and prevention for all cancers. David and Carolyn Mandel David and Carolyn Mandel, through the Mandel Family Fund, have generously pledged $100,000 to support targeted treatment research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia (WM) under Steven P. Treon, MD, PhD, Robert F. Tannenhauser Chair for Waldenström’s Research at Dana-Farber. Their gift will help develop more precise therapies to improve care for WM patients worldwide. Frank Marshall Frank Marshall will make a future bequest of $250,000 to support the research of Paul Richardson, MD, the R.J. Corman Professor of Medicine at Harvard Medical School and Dana-Farber. Frank’s thoughtful estate gift will help drive scientific discovery, advance more effective therapies, and improve outcomes for patients with this complex blood cancer. Walter and Gail McCormick Having been inspired by matching opportunities in the past, Walter and Gail McCormick made an unrestricted gift of $250,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to match donations made in summer 2026. Through their generous support of cancer research and patient care, they are advancing lifesaving work at Dana-Farber and encouraging others to make a lasting difference. National Breast Cancer Foundation National Breast Cancer Foundation has made generous gifts totaling $155,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute furthering their ongoing support of breast cancer prevention, screening, and treatment, and related community health initiatives. This latest gift is pivotal to advancing our mission to defy cancer and provide equitable care. Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation Chiara Mazziotta, PhD, received a $100,000 Mentored Research Award from The Neuroendocrine Tumor Research Foundation to investigate proteins and pathways involved in the development of Merkel cell carcinoma. This work can help generate insights that lead to innovative treatment strategies. Specifically, she will examine how YAP/TAZ and mTOR influence disease progression. Rally Against Cancer Fundraising teams around New England raised $142,000 through Rally Against Cancer to help Dana-Farber Cancer Institute strike out cancer. Teams also won prizes and celebrated the start of baseball season on Fenway Opening Day. SebastianStrong Foundation The SebastianStrong Foundation awarded Cigall Kadoch, PhD, a $332,877 grant to conduct research to inform the development of small molecules targeting the SS18-SSX fusion in synovial sarcoma. This award honors Sebastian, who was fifteen when diagnosed with rhabdomyosarcoma, by offering hope through the development of more innovative treatments. Daniel Tamkin and Lucinda Cardinal Daniel Tamkin and Lucinda Cardinal pledged $250,000 to establish a fund for testicular cancer research in memory of Kyle S. Bhatiya. Their generosity honors Kyle’s life while advancing the work of Alok Tewari, MD, PhD, to better understand and overcome treatment resistance. Nicole Walsh Fall 2026By Casey Repasy A $100,000 gift from Nicole Walsh to the Walsh Family Fund is supporting the research of Sahar Nissim, MD, PhD, focused on pioneering approaches to intercept pancreatic cancer before it develops. The funding will support the study of precancerous lesions and their progression to invasive cancer, providing critical insights to guide new strategies for cancer interception. Load More Briefs Summer 2026 Zlotoff Generations Fund The Zlotoff Generations Fund gifted $250,000 toward a partnership between Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Ichilov, the Tel Aviv Sourasky University Medical Center, Israel’s leading academic medical center and largest public acute care facility. This generosity will support research in AI and advanced breast cancer, as well as work in early detection and clinical education. American-Italian Cancer Foundation Dana-Farber Cancer Institute received generous support from the American-Italian Cancer Foundation that will help fund three important research opportunities. Each researcher received $60,000. The funds will further the work of Francesco Corrado, MD, developing immunotherapies in multiple myeloma; Carmine Valenza, MD, for his research on hormone receptor-positive breast cancer; and Valentina Santo, MD, for her research of non-small cell lung cancer. Andrew McDonough B+ Foundation The Andrew McDonough B+ Foundation awarded $100,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Steven DuBois, MD, MS, and his research evaluating antibody-drug conjugate targets in children with relapsed solid and central nervous system tumors. This critical work could expand treatment options and help personalize care for pediatric patients. Brian and Elizabeth Rutledge Summer 2026By Tarice GrayPhotography by Michael Blanchard Brian and Elizabeth Rutledge made a $300,000 gift supporting research focused on Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia (WM). Shayna Sarosiek, MD, and her colleagues are committed to improving the quality of life and patient outcomes for those with the disease. This gift will allow the team to expand, adding a dedicated research assistant for the neuropathy project, to track how WM-associated neuropathy changes over time and evaluate treatment options. Kenneth and Jodi Bring A heartfelt $100,000 gift made by Kenneth and Jodi Bring will support gastrointestinal cancer research in loving memory of Jodi's mother, Reesa Cohen. This generous philanthropic gift empowers the efforts of Brian Wolpin, MD, MPH, the Robert T. & Judith B. Hale Chair in Pancreatic Cancer at Dana-Farber, to advance studies focused on early detection and developing improved treatments, honoring Cohen’s legacy while transforming care for patients facing these challenging cancers. Cancer Research Society The Cancer Research Society awarded a grant of $185,000 to support the breast cancer research of Marie-Anne Goyette, PhD. Her project explores cancer cells that become more aggressive and resistant to treatments because of increased sugar layers on their surface. By studying the enzymes responsible for these abnormal sugars, Goyette seeks to develop new therapeutic strategies to improve breast cancer patient outcomes. Cannonball Kids’ Cancer Cannonball Kids’ Cancer awarded Dana-Farber a $200,000 Andy Albert Next Step Clinical Trial Grant to support Allison O’Neill, MD, in advancing next-generation treatments for relapsed pediatric solid tumors. Her team is testing a new antibody treatment and combination therapy which has the potential to improve patient care and outcomes. Crystal Family Charitable Foundation The Crystal Family Charitable Foundation has continued their longstanding support of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s patient care programs and research areas. Most recently, the foundation provided a gift of $125,000 to support initiatives that advance Dana-Farber's total patient care model, including the Bereavement Program, Holiday Patient Assistance Program, and novel investigations in onco-fertility and pediatric liver cancer research. The Skinny Pig Fund Keith Salome’s family founded The Skinny Pig Fund to support kidney cancer research after his renal cell cancer diagnosis. Sadly, Keith passed away in September of 2024. Determined to make a difference, his family continues to raise funds and awareness in Keith’s name, raising over $100,000 in just 14 months. Through fundraising opportunities like the Jimmy Fund Walk for Dana-Farber presented by Hyundai, the Boston Marathon®, the New York City Marathon, and more, Team Skinny Pig is well on their way towards their ultimate goal of $1 million. Elizabeth Bein Elizabeth Bein gave a generous gift of $120,000 to establish the Bein Family Fund for Lynch Syndrome Research. The fund will be managed by Matthew B. Yurgelun, MD, FASCO, CGAF. Yurgelen’s team carries out essential early phase work designed to detect early stage urinary cancers, specifically for patients with Lynch syndrome. Gerry and Sherry Cohen A generous $100,000 gift from Sherry and Gerry Cohen to fuel cancer research, prevention, and treatment efforts made an incredible, dual impact by also inspiring community support through Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Winter Matching Challenge. Their steadfast contributions, combined with the groundswell of additional matching appeal donations, have resulted in $1.7 million raised since 2021. Jeffrey T. Spear Trust The Jeffrey T. Spear Trust has given $419,559 to support cancer care and research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Jeff and his wife Gail’s generosity will support Dana-Farber’s dedication to developing innovative cancer treatments and providing the highest-quality care. Meaningful legacy gifts like this will ultimately help advance Dana-Farber programs, resources, and services for cancer patients and their families. Shafran Haimes Foundation’s gift for CLL The Shafran Haimes Foundation is supporting chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) research led by Jennifer Brown, MD, PhD, and the Worthington and Margaret Collette Professor of Medicine in the Field of Hematologic Oncology at Harvard Medical School. The generous gift of $150,000 will help fund Brown’s work analyzing minimal residual disease in patients with CLL to help determine the effectiveness of existing treatment options and develop new care strategies. LUNGevity Foundation The LUNGevity Foundation, in partnership with the EGFR Resisters, recently made a $300,000 gift to Dana-Farber’s Elliot Brea, MD, PhD. This gift demonstrates the foundation’s deep commitment to Brea’s growth, furthering his research of CAR T treatments in non-small cell lung cancer and development of new therapies to improve outcomes for patients with lung cancer. Mrs. Maryellen Maguire-Eisen and Dr. Richard Eisen Maryellen and Richard have pledged $100,000 for nursing education at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, helping to address the growing need for skilled oncology nurses. This generous gift builds on Maryellen’s own remarkable legacy as a Dana-Farber nurse and supports programs led by Anne Gross, PhD, RN, NEA-BC, FAAN, which empower nurses at every stage of their careers—ultimately elevating care for patients. Mark Geer Retired psychologist Mark Geer, EdD, included a $125,000 gift to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in his estate plans in gratitude for the care he received while being treated for two cancers. Describing his experience at Dana-Farber as exceptional, he directed his bequest to patient care and research. Max Kade Foundation The Max Kade Foundation made gifts totaling $156,000 to support the postdoctoral fellowship work of Lara Engertsberger, MD, mentored by Mariella Filbin, MD, PhD, and Angelika Starzer, MD. These gifts will enable Engertsberger and Starzer to gain crucial cancer research experience in Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s world-class labs to expand their knowledge and skills. National Cancer Center National Cancer Center awarded two new postdoctoral fellowships to Dana-Farber researchers Shelby Roseman, PhD, and Kaiwen Sun, PhD, and has renewed second-year funding for Katharina Hoebel, MD, PhD, and Diego Martinez Alonso, PhD. This support totals $488,000 and enables these investigators to pursue innovative cancer research and strengthens their path towards independent research careers, helping accelerate discoveries that improve outcomes for patients worldwide PMC 25/50 Pan-Mass Challenge weekend has several same-day routes including the PMC 25/50. On Aug. 2, riders may choose a 25- or 50-mile loop and participate in festivities at the finish in Wellesley. The PMC is Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s single largest supporter, and 100% of every rider-raised dollar goes to Dana-Farber. Please visit pmc.org to learn more. Salgi Esophageal Cancer Research Foundation The Salgi Esophageal Cancer Research Foundation has awarded more than $263,000 to support Dana-Farber investigators Haeseong Park, MD, PhD, and Masood Shamas, PhD. This funding will drive studies into disease progression, treatment resistance, and novel drug targets in esophageal adenocarcinoma, offering renewed hope and transformative possibilities for patients facing this rising cancer challenge. The Stenson Foundation Dana-Farber Cancer Institute’s Lindsay Frazier, MD, received a $100,000 award from The Stenson Foundation to develop germ cell tumor models, which may unlock new treatment options for pediatric and adolescent patients. Their support honors Charlie, a two-time germ cell cancer survivor, whose courage continues to inspire the Foundation’s work. The Michael & Helen R. Cyker Charitable Foundation The Michael & Helen R. Cyker Charitable Foundation is providing $100,000 in flexible funding for leukemia research. Daniel DeAngelo, MD, PhD, leads the team that is focused on new and effective treatments for patients with leukemia. This tremendous gift will go towards efforts to improve outcomes and ultimately ease the burden of cancer for patients. William G. Pomeroy Foundation William G. Pomeroy and the Wiliam G. Pomeroy Foundation generously made gifts totaling $400,000 to fuel research in stem cell transplantation. Of that gift amount, $350,000 was given to the William G. Hope Scarves Daniel Abravanel, MD, PhD, received $115,000 from Hope Scarves in 2023 to support his investigations on the evolution of metastatic breast tumors and the mechanisms they use to evade treatment. This work promises to help transform the treatment of the disease in years to come. Innovation in Cancer Informatics Innovation in Cancer Informatics awarded $224,000 to support investigations led by Sylvan Baca, MD, PhD, and Eliezer Van Allen, MD, into circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). This research will analyze tumor features and aims to, for the first time, guide therapy selection in breast cancer with low levels of ctDNA. The Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research The Jane Coffin Childs Memorial Fund for Medical Research gave a generous grant to support research by Jose Orozco, MD, PhD, into the role of sugar-sensing pathways in metabolic adaptation. These studies may reveal a new therapeutic target to alleviate metabolic maladaptive responses to the chronic overconsumption of sugars and carbohydrates. Keep Smiling Beautiful Keep Smiling Beautiful is a 5K race hosted by the family of Chelsea Smith, to champion research into hepatocellular carcinoma—liver cancer—by Chelsea’s doctor, Allison O’Neill, MD, at Dana-Farber. Each year, in Chelsea’s honor, O’Neill runs this 5K which has raised more than $115,000 since 2017. Michael and Margaret Kerr Michael and Margaret Kerr established the Kerr Family Fund for Translational Research at Dana-Farber with a $100,000 gift in 2023. The fund will be directed by James Cleary, MD, PhD, whom the couple laud for his compassionate patient care. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy A new $1 million gift from Rev. Dr. Priscilla Lawrence and Patrick MeLampy will advance the work of Irene Ghobrial, MD, a Lavine Family Chair for Preventative Cancer Therapies at Dana-Farber, and the Center for Early Detection and Interception of Blood Cancers to better understand risk factors for multiple myeloma and develop interventions to stop the disease from progressing. Jimmy Fund Little League Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports raised $281,332 in 2023 for cancer research and care at Dana-Farber. Every year, Little League baseball and softball players in New England raise vital funds for the Jimmy Fund during this summer league, making a significant impact in the fight against cancer. Brenda McAdam After being diagnosed with cholangiocarcinoma, a rare bile duct cancer, in August 2022, Brenda McAdam established the Brenda McAdam Fund for Bile Duct Cancer Research at Dana-Farber under the direction of James Cleary, MD, PhD. With her $100,000 gift, she hopes Cleary can help patients like her defy this rare cancer. National Cancer Center Five Dana-Farber investigators were recently awarded more than $250,000 from the National Cancer Center (NCC), whose mission is to provide financial support to researchers undertaking innovative and promising studies that seek to cure cancer. Since its founding 70 years ago, NCC has granted nearly $8 million in cancer research funding. National Comprehensive Cancer Network The National Comprehensive Cancer Network made a generous grant of $250,000 to support lung cancer screening led by Mary Cooley, PhD, RN, FAAN. The grant will help to optimize early detection efforts among patients, providers, and across the health care system. Oligo Nation Dana-Farber recently received a $100,000 grant from Oligo Nation to advance vital research on oligodendroglioma, a rare type of brain tumor. This grant propels efforts to develop treatment strategies to target dependencies conferred by IDH oncogenes in this disease. One Mission In 2023, One Mission contributed $189,000 to Dana-Farber, reinforcing its long-standing dedication to pediatric cancer patients. This contribution enhances the wellbeing of young patients through the Pediatric Resource Program as well as family-centered initiatives like the Jimmy Fund Clinic Festival, a Parent Bereavement cruise, and other special events for patients at the Jimmy Fund Clinic. Pancreatic Cancer Action Network With their latest commitment of $300,000, the Pancreatic Cancer Action Network is supporting the work of Dana-Farber’s Andrew Aguirre, MD, PhD, who aims to identify the mechanisms of response or resistance to a combination treatment for pancreatic cancer. Thoracic Foundation Spring 2024By Colleen SullivanPhotography courtesy of the Thoracic Foundation The Thoracic Foundation awarded grants totaling $160,000 to Dana-Farber in 2023, to honor the wishes of foundation trustee Bradley Cook, who passed away in 2022. Brad, alongside his peers at the Thoracic Foundation, has been a steady funder of thoracic cancer research and instrumental in the nearly $900,000 the foundation has given over the years to Dana-Farber. Polly and Ming Tsai Spring 2024By Lori DoughertyPhotography courtesy of the Tsai family Polly and Ming Tsai made a generous new commitment to advance research by David Barbie, MD, and the Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology designed to increase the durability, precision, and effectiveness of lung cancer treatments, like the promising CAR T-cell therapy already in development with previous support from the Tsais. Aaron Yuan With a gift of $100,000, Aaron Yuan established a fund in honor of his mother, Chaochi Yuan, to support BOLSTER, an educational and support program for ovarian cancer patients and caregivers led by Chaochi’s oncologist, Alexi Wright, MD, MPH; and to expand the program to include translation into Mandarin Chinese. Load More Briefs Winter 2023 Jonathan and Hope Ashner A generous $100,000 gift from Jonathan and Hope Ashner was made to support the research of Elizabeth Buchbinder, MD. The gift will help to fuel Buchbinder’s groundbreaking investigations into melanoma and maximize progress against the disease. Doron Broman Doron Broman, a Miami-based real estate developer and stage IV pancreatic cancer patient, has given $150,000 to support research in pancreatic cancer under the direction of Kimmie Ng, MD, MPH. Broman came to Dana-Farber in 2015 with only months to live, but under the treatment of Ng, has defied the odds and is celebrating seven years since his diagnosis. Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein Jeffrey and Jennifer Goldstein made a generous gift in support of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole M. and Philip L. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology at Dana-Farber. The gift will support Jänne and his team’s continued research into targeted therapies in lung cancer, novel EGFR inhibitors, and mechanisms of drug resistance, ultimately helping more patients and their families. Matthew Miller Matthew Miller gave $100,000 to advance groundbreaking investigations in melanoma led by Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Miller’s support will help Haq uncover the genomic intricacies of drug resistance and explore new ways to enhance personalized medicine for patients. National Foundation for Cancer Research Dana-Farber recently received a $110,000 grant from the National Foundation for Cancer Research to study new, non-invasive approaches to identify specific subtypes of kidney cancer and particular genetic alterations in prostate cancer, with the aim of creating earlier detection and treatment interventions for patients with these diseases. Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation The Terri Brodeur Breast Cancer Foundation recently made grants totaling $200,000 to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute to fund two studies. One explores circulating tumor DNA at critical timepoints in early stage hormone receptor-positive breast cancer, and the second assesses how chemotherapy effects the tumor-immune microenvironment and estrogen receptor activity in young women with hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Load More Briefs Fall 2023 American Association for Cancer Research The American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) recently awarded $480,000 to four Dana-Farber physician-scientists who are investigating new methods of prevention, diagnosis, and treatment for various types of cancers. As the first cancer research organization dedicated to preventing and curing cancer, AACR is a long-standing partner in Dana-Farber’s mission to defy cancer. American Federation for Aging Research The Glenn Foundation for Medical Research and the American Federation for Aging Research awarded a $300,000 grant to support basic science research by Dana-Farber’s Edward Chouchani, PhD, as he seeks to systematically define the functional targets of reactive oxygen species that contribute to longevity and age. B.A.A. 5K® The B.A.A. 5K® took place April 15, welcoming the largest team to date of Dana-Farber runners who collectively raised $184,271. Runners had the option to race in person on the 3.1-mile course that began and ended in the Boston Common, or run in their own neighborhoods as virtual teammates. The top fundraiser honor went to David Mullen. Richard and Sandra Bornstein Sandra Bornstein and her late husband, Richard, made a generous commitment of $400,000 to support early career physician-scientists on the leukemia and stem cell transplant teams at Dana-Farber. Faculty excellence is a top priority of The Dana-Farber Campaign, and this funding will help fuel the growth of promising investigators as they work to ensure greater numbers of patients live longer, healthier lives. Clifford Family The Clifford Family established the Woolley-Clifford Foundation Fund with a $100,000 gift, supporting the research of David Kozono, MD, PhD, as he works to investigate blood and tissue-based biomarkers in lung cancer patients that can help predict lung inflammation and anti-tumor response following radiation therapy. Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation The Harold and Janice Cohen Foundation made a generous $150,000 gift in support of lifelong friend Richard M. Stone, MD, the Lunder Family Chair in Leukemia at Dana-Farber. The gift will advance Stone’s research to identify novel targets in acute leukemia and myelodysplastic syndromes. Colorectal Cancer Alliance The Colorectal Cancer Alliance made a $150,000 grant to Dana-Farber to fund research into new treatments for colorectal cancer, the third most common type of cancer worldwide. Building on previous research, a Dana-Farber team is working to develop a novel class of therapeutics designed to promote cancer cell death by inducing cancer cell maturation. Conquer Cancer Conquer Cancer,® the ASCO Foundation, awarded $600,000 worth of grants to support studies addressing cancer care disparities in clinical trial enrollment for pediatric patients, and exploring new treatment options for prostate cancer that can reduce the chance of recurrence. The Dana Foundation Our historic partner, the Dana Foundation, made a new $100,000 commitment to the Defy Cancer Fund, which provides unrestricted support for The Dana-Farber Campaign. These flexible funds propel innovative early stage research, speed new drugs into clinical trials, retain and attract top talent; meet unanticipated needs; and ensure that we are fully serving our patients’ physical, emotional, psychological, and spiritual needs. Friends of Dana-Farber Annual Gala The Friends of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute recently held their Annual Gala, raising more than $465,000. Evening with Friends featured cocktails, dinner, and a live auction. The Friends exemplify the “power of friends” through their dual mission: raising funds to support research, patient services, breast and gynecologic cancer programs, and oncology fellowships; and providing services that enhance Dana-Farber's healing environment. Gastric Cancer Foundation The Gastric Cancer Foundation gave $100,000 to support the research of Dana-Farber’s Nilay Sethi, MD, PhD, who is investigating treatments for gastric cancers with homologous recombination (HR) deficiencies that have proven effective in other types of HR-deficient cancers. Greenwall Foundation The Greenwall Foundation made a generous grant of more than $240,000 to support a Dana-Farber-led study into sustainability and conservation ethics in clinical decision-making, as part of the foundation’s mission to make bioethics an integral part of health care, policy, and research. Innovation in Cancer Informatics With a $224,000 grant, Innovation in Cancer Informatics is funding a project at Dana-Farber that will develop and pilot a new mobile health application that integrates patients’ electronic health records to better support them, and their care teams, in management of advanced cancer pain. Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway In June, adult and pediatric patients and their families joined donors and sponsors for a once-in-a-lifetime chance to step up to the plate at Fenway Park. Jimmy Fund Day at Fenway presented by DraftKings raised $223,000 thanks to stand-out fundraisers like Team Russo and many others giving generously to strike out cancer. Jay and Kristy Ladieu Jay and Kristy Ladieu gave $125,000 to support melanoma research under the direction of Megan Insco, MD, PhD, at Dana-Farber. Fueled by this gift, Insco and her team are pursuing studies into the biology of melanoma, laying the groundwork for critically needed treatment options. Martha Massey Martha Massey increased a recent pledge by $100,000 to support the research of Robert Soiffer, MD, the Worthington and Margaret Collette Professor of Medicine. In memory of her beloved husband, Calvin, Massey’s expanded support enables Soiffer to further research in the drug venetoclax for hematologic malignancies. Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance Ovarian cancer is often difficult to treat at later stages and difficult to detect at earlier stages. With a $100,000 grant, the Minnesota Ovarian Cancer Alliance is supporting research at Dana-Farber into the development of an ultrasensitive blood test to detect ovarian cancer at its earliest, and most treatable, stages. Mugar Foundation The Mugar Foundation made a generous commitment of $500,000 to support the previously established Mugar Family Fellowship in Lung Cancer. While advancing promising lung cancer research, the fellowship provides reliable funding for an early career scientist to pursue innovative research and develop the skills needed to lead the future of lung cancer research. Prostate Cancer Research Prostate Cancer Research gave nearly $400,000 in support of a Dana-Farber study that aims to improve prostate cancer screening equity. Researchers will analyze the impact of community-targeted interventions to reduce barriers to screening in Black men with prostate cancer. Robert Wood Johnson Foundation Dana-Farber’s Temidayo Fadelu, MD, MPH, received the Harold Amos Medical Faculty Development Award, a program of the Robert Wood Johnson Foundation in partnership with the Indiana University School of Medicine. Jeff Silveira and Beth Logan In memory of their dear friend, Melanie Rosay, Jeff Silveira and Beth Logan recently made a $250,000 gift toward the Melanie Rosay Fund for Breast Cancer Research at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. The fund, established in 2020 through gifts from friends and family of Melanie, seeks to raise $1 million to provide support for metastatic breast cancer research under Dana-Farber’s Rinath Jeselsohn, MD. Strike Out Cancer with the Jimmy Fund As the Red Sox returned to Fenway Park this spring, the Jimmy Fund community came together to cheer them on and support Dana-Farber patients. Rally Against CancerSM teams celebrated Opening Day on March 30 and more than 100 fans signed up to strike out cancer by donating for every Red Sox win, raising $240,000 in total. Go, Sox! William Randolph Hearst Foundations The William Randolph Hearst Foundations gave $200,000 to fund two one-year Nurse Practitioner Adult Palliative Care Fellowships at Dana-Farber, to support two nurse practitioners in the Department of Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care, where the focus on treating the whole person—mind, body, and spirit—helps provide patients with relief from the symptoms, pain, and stress of a serious illness. Li Xu Li Xu, MD, MS, MBA, made a $100,000 gift in memory of her parents, Drs. Zhen-Quan Xu and Lin Yuan (pictured), to support pioneering lung cancer research under the direction of Pasi Jänne, MD, PhD, director of the Carole L. and Philip M. Lowe Center for Thoracic Oncology and of the Robert and Renée Belfer Center for Applied Cancer Science at Dana-Farber. Load More Briefs Summer 2023 20 Years of Survivorship In 2022, Andrea McGrath celebrated 20 years since her successful stem cell transplant at Dana-Farber. She hosted a survivorship event, raising over $16,000 to benefit the work of her doctor and now friend, Corey Cutler, MD, MPH, FRCPC, whose advances in stem cell transplantation are continuing to improve outcomes for blood disorder patients like her. 3000 Miles to a Cure 3000 Miles to a Cure awarded $100,000 to support the ALLELE-GBM research program at Dana-Farber, under the direction of Keith Ligon, MD, PhD. Ligon’s team is working to put genomic data into the hands of patients, providers, and researchers to advance treatments and clinical trials in glioblastoma (GBM). Barbara and Arnold Barron Barbara and Arnold Barron gave $100,000 to support lung cancer research under the direction of Michael Rabin, MD. The couple has supported the work of Rabin and Dana-Farber for many years, this gift marking their latest commitment to spur advancements in durable treatments for lung cancer patients at Dana-Farber and around the globe. Charles A. King Trust The Charles A. King Trust Postdoctoral Research Fellowship Program, administered by Health Resources in Action, awarded grants totaling $246,776 to two Dana-Farber fellows working in small cell lung cancer and leukemia, as part of the trust’s mission to promote the investigation of human disease, to alleviate suffering through improved treatment. Children’s Cancer Research Fund Children’s Cancer Research Fund awarded their Emerging Scientist Award to Dana-Farber pediatric oncologist Emily Heikamp, MD, PhD, MSc. The grant of $100,000 will support Heikamp’s work in uncovering therapeutic vulnerabilities in the NU98-r gene, which could lead to safer and more effective treatments for children with relapsed acute myeloid leukemia. Joe Connolly Joe Connolly established the Deborah Connolly Small Cell Lung Cancer Research Fund at Dana-Farber in honor of his late wife, with a gift of $100,000. The fund will support research such as studies of the molecular mutations driving small cell lung cancer, with the goal of developing targeted therapies. The Foley Family The Foley Family made a gift of $100,000 to advance research into paragangliomas, a rare type of neuroendocrine tumor, led by Kimberly Perez, MD. Their gift will support experimental studies including the first clinical trial analyzing better treatments for patients with hereditary and non-hereditary paragangliomas. Haymakers for Hope In September 2022, 24 women stepped into the ring to deliver a knockout against cancer at Haymakers for Hope’s Belles of the Brawl amateur boxing event at MGM Music Hall in Boston’s Fenway area. The bout raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and gave women who have been affected by cancer an opportunity to fight back. Kicks for Cancer Each September, the Concord-Carlisle High School community in Concord, Mass., comes together for Kicks for Cancer, an opportunity for area high school sports teams to support Dr. Dipanjan Chowdhury's Ovarian Cancer Early Detection Fund. The 2022 event raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and honored students’ loved ones who have faced cancer. Mulligan Family Fundraiser The Mulligan Family organized a birthday fundraiser for Dana-Farber in honor of their loved one, Patrick. They raised over $15,000 to help James Cleary, MD, PhD, standardize screening options and uncover more effective treatments for pancreatic cancer. One Mission One Mission recently demonstrated its commitment to cancer patients with two gifts totaling nearly $220,000 in support of the Blum Pediatric Resource Room and Pediatric Resource Program at Dana-Farber. One Mission, founded in 2008 by Ashley and Ari Haseotes, aims to help families cope with the emotional and financial challenges brought on by childhood cancer. Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research The Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research awarded $300,000 in grants to support exploring liquid biopsies to advance precision treatment; uncovering causes of drug resistance in relapsed neuroblastoma; analyzing the proteins that drive medulloblastoma; and testing nanoparticle delivery of targeted therapy in diffuse midline gliomas to lay the groundwork for clinical trials. Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation A $300,000 Odyssey Award from the Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation provides critical resources to develop a groundbreaking platform to analyze the structure and function of disordered proteins that drive disease progression. This pioneering project promises to reveal structural biological insights while validating a powerful new tool to inform drug discovery across multiple cancers. Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation The Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation awarded $200,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into how aging affects the behavior of tumor cells. This research, led by Lewis Cantley, PhD, in the Department of Cancer Biology, could provide further insight that may inform the development of age-specific treatment approaches for cancer. St. Baldrick’s Foundation St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood brain cancer. Tap Cancer Out Tap Cancer Out, a jiu-jitsu based nonprofit raising awareness and funds for cancer fighting organizations on behalf of the grappling community, recently made a $100,000 gift to support innovative research by Rizwan Romee, MD, into novel immunotherapeutic approaches for breast cancer at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Load More Briefs Spring 2023 Margaret and Michael Bayer Margaret and Michael Bayer gave $100,000 to establish The Bayer Family Research Fund. The fund aims to accelerate discoveries into safer, more effective and durable treatments for patients facing Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a rare form of blood cancer. Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award The 2022 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to John Berardi (second from right), program director of Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports, which rallies thousands of youth baseball and softball players each summer to fundraise for the Jimmy Fund in their communities and has raised over $6 million for Dana-Farber since 1986. Breast Cancer Alliance Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such as immunotherapy. Fred and Michele Brettschneider Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. Burlingame Foundation The Burlingame Foundation gave $300,000 to provide support for patient navigation through the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP). Patient navigation involves supporting and assisting patients through the complexities of treatment—a key component of the CCEP’s effort to address disparities in cancer care. Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament The annual Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament raised more than $40,000 in 2022, a new record, to support the Adult Survivorship Program in the Perini Family Survivors’ Center at Dana-Farber. The tournament draws 38 teams and more than 470 participants from 11 states to raise funds to ensure a healthy quality of life after cancer. Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program graduates and panelists (from left): Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, program director and the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber; Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, EVP, head of global product development and chief medical officer, Roche and Genentech; and Nadine McCleary, MD, MPH, medical director, Patient Reported Data Program at Dana-Farber. David Liposarcoma Research Initiative In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of George Demetri, MD, director of the Sarcoma Center, senior vice president of Experimental Therapeutics, and the Quick Family Chair in Medical Oncology at Dana-Farber. Pictured (from left) at the event: George Demetri, MD, with Nicole Solimini, PhD, and Greg David of the Rossy Foundation. Emerald Foundation, Inc. Emerald Foundation, Inc., awarded $300,000 to support research harnessing natural killer (NK) cells for use in immunotherapies. NK cells play a major role in the elimination of both tumors and infected cells, and this research will provide valuable insight that will inform better treatment strategies. A Celebration for the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber Supporters gathered to celebrate the recently established Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber. The endowed Chair was funded by colleagues, mentees, grateful patients, family, and friends in honor of Robert J. Mayer, MD, who served as director of the Fellowship Program for more than 35 years. Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, who succeeded Mayer as director, was appointed the first incumbent. Pictured (from left): Mayer, LaCasce, and Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD. Richard and Eileen Greisch Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches. Holiday Patient Assistance The Holiday Patient Assistance Program, which helps patients and families in critical financial need, raised $192,785 in 2022. The program helped 726 eligible Dana-Farber patients and families celebrate the season by providing gift cards to help cover the cost of expenses like gas to travel to appointments, groceries for holiday meals, and small gifts for loved ones. Jog for Julie The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber. Michele and Howard Kessler Institute Trustee Michele Kessler and her husband, Howard Kessler, made a gift of $250,000 to launch the Cannabis Care Support Program at Dana-Farber, which aims to create sustainable oncologic cannabis educational resources and advance research on the use of cannabis to address the mental and physical side effects of cancer. Lymphoma Research Foundation As part of their mission to fund innovative research at top institutions around the country, the Lymphoma Research Foundation’s recent funding cycle included awarding grants totaling $115,000 to fund two Dana-Farber studies into advanced treatment options for patients diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma and mantle cell lymphoma. Max Vincze Foundation With a $100,000 grant, the Max Vincze Foundation established a fund to support research into NUT carcinoma, a rare cancer, in honor of Max Vincze, who passed away from the disease in 2021 at the age of 23. National Palliative Care Research Center The National Palliative Care Research Center awarded $198,000 to support the creation of a program to develop nurse-led psychosocial intervention for historically marginalized pediatric patients, with the goal of improving family-centered communication and pediatric patients’ quality of life during treatment. Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Poorvu Jaffe Chair Celebration James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at a celebration in November 2022 are (standing, from left) Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; Institute Trustee Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel Jaffe; and Tulsky; (seated) Lia and Bill Poorvu. Quest 2 Defy Cancer Over 30 streamers and content creators from around the U.S. participated in the latest Quest 2 Defy Cancer. The program, part of the Jimmy Fund Let's Game® initiative, invites streamers, gamers, and content creators to make an impact on the lifesaving work happening at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Swim Across America For 27 years, Swim Across America has supported Dana-Farber through events like their annual Boston Open Water Swim event. In 2022, swimmers of all ages and skill levels raised $142,000 to help support cancer research and care at the Institute, for a lifetime total of more than $3 million. Ware Estate James W. Ware left a generous gift of $334,745 to provide unrestricted support for research and care at Dana-Farber. Unrestricted gifts provide flexible support for programs throughout Dana-Farber, from innovative basic research, to clinical trials, to programs that enhance the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care. William Raveis Ride + Walk The annual William Raveis Ride + Walk raised $115,000 for Dana-Farber in 2022. This event is the largest fundraiser put on by employees from William Raveis Real Estate across New England, New York, and Florida. Load More Briefs
