Haymakers for Hope In September 2022, 24 women stepped into the ring to deliver a knockout against cancer at Haymakers for Hope’s Belles of the Brawl amateur boxing event at MGM Music Hall in Boston’s Fenway area. The bout raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and gave women who have been affected by cancer an opportunity to fight back. Kicks for Cancer Each September, the Concord-Carlisle High School community in Concord, Mass., comes together for Kicks for Cancer, an opportunity for area high school sports teams to support Dr. Dipanjan Chowdhury's Ovarian Cancer Early Detection Fund. The 2022 event raised $116,000 for Dana-Farber and honored students’ loved ones who have faced cancer. Mulligan Family Fundraiser The Mulligan Family organized a birthday fundraiser for Dana-Farber in honor of their loved one, Patrick. They raised over $15,000 to help James Cleary, MD, PhD, standardize screening options and uncover more effective treatments for pancreatic cancer. One Mission One Mission recently demonstrated its commitment to cancer patients with two gifts totaling nearly $220,000 in support of the Blum Pediatric Resource Room and Pediatric Resource Program at Dana-Farber. One Mission, founded in 2008 by Ashley and Ari Haseotes, aims to help families cope with the emotional and financial challenges brought on by childhood cancer. Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research The Rally Foundation for Childhood Cancer Research awarded $300,000 in grants to support exploring liquid biopsies to advance precision treatment; uncovering causes of drug resistance in relapsed neuroblastoma; analyzing the proteins that drive medulloblastoma; and testing nanoparticle delivery of targeted therapy in diffuse midline gliomas to lay the groundwork for clinical trials. Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation A $300,000 Odyssey Award from the Richard and Susan Smith Family Foundation provides critical resources to develop a groundbreaking platform to analyze the structure and function of disordered proteins that drive disease progression. This pioneering project promises to reveal structural biological insights while validating a powerful new tool to inform drug discovery across multiple cancers. Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation The Samuel Waxman Cancer Research Foundation awarded $200,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into how aging affects the behavior of tumor cells. This research, led by Lewis Cantley, PhD, in the Department of Cancer Biology, could provide further insight that may inform the development of age-specific treatment approaches for cancer. St. Baldrick’s Foundation St. Baldrick’s Foundation awarded a total of $415,000 to Dana-Farber studies into how neuroblastoma, one of the most common pediatric solid tumors, escapes destruction by the immune system; and how a category of newly discovered “dark proteins” may point toward new approaches to treat medulloblastoma, a devastating form of childhood brain cancer. Tap Cancer Out Tap Cancer Out, a jiu-jitsu based nonprofit raising awareness and funds for cancer fighting organizations on behalf of the grappling community, recently made a $100,000 gift to support innovative research by Rizwan Romee, MD, into novel immunotherapeutic approaches for breast cancer at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Load More Briefs Spring 2023 Margaret and Michael Bayer Margaret and Michael Bayer gave $100,000 to establish The Bayer Family Research Fund. The fund aims to accelerate discoveries into safer, more effective and durable treatments for patients facing Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia, a rare form of blood cancer. Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award The 2022 Boston Red Sox Jimmy Fund Award—the Jimmy Fund’s highest honor—was presented to John Berardi (second from right), program director of Jimmy Fund Little League presented by Franklin Sports, which rallies thousands of youth baseball and softball players each summer to fundraise for the Jimmy Fund in their communities and has raised over $6 million for Dana-Farber since 1986. Breast Cancer Alliance Breast Cancer Alliance awarded $125,000 to Dana-Farber to support research into the features of the tumor microenvironment that result in metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC). This work will improve researchers’ knowledge of the behavior of TNBC and may help identify patients who are more likely to benefit from treatments such as immunotherapy. Fred and Michele Brettschneider Fred and Michele Brettschneider made a commitment of $250,000 to support a clinical trial network for Waldenström’s macroglobulinemia and advance all clinical research for this rare form of blood cancer within the Bing Center for Waldenström’s Macroglobulinemia. Burlingame Foundation The Burlingame Foundation gave $300,000 to provide support for patient navigation through the Cancer Care Equity Program (CCEP). Patient navigation involves supporting and assisting patients through the complexities of treatment—a key component of the CCEP’s effort to address disparities in cancer care. Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament The annual Cross-Check Cancer Women’s Hockey Tournament raised more than $40,000 in 2022, a new record, to support the Adult Survivorship Program in the Perini Family Survivors’ Center at Dana-Farber. The tournament draws 38 teams and more than 470 participants from 11 states to raise funds to ensure a healthy quality of life after cancer. Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium In October, Dana-Farber supporters and leaders gathered for the annual Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Presidential Symposium. Attendees received firsthand updates on the State of the Institute, advances and opportunities in prevention and early detection, the impact of philanthropy on advancing research, and Dana-Farber’s world-renowned hematology/oncology fellowship program. Pictured are fellowship program graduates and panelists (from left): Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, program director and the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber; Levi Garraway, MD, PhD, EVP, head of global product development and chief medical officer, Roche and Genentech; and Nadine McCleary, MD, MPH, medical director, Patient Reported Data Program at Dana-Farber. David Liposarcoma Research Initiative In September, the inaugural David Liposarcoma Research Initiative International Scientific Symposium was held at Dana-Farber. The symposium included the unveiling of a plaque commemorating the generous pledge from the Rossy Foundation that, through The Rossy Foundation Fund at KBF Canada, established the David Liposarcoma Research Initiative under the direction of George Demetri, MD, director of the Sarcoma Center, senior vice president of Experimental Therapeutics, and the Quick Family Chair in Medical Oncology at Dana-Farber. Pictured (from left) at the event: George Demetri, MD, with Nicole Solimini, PhD, and Greg David of the Rossy Foundation. Emerald Foundation, Inc. Emerald Foundation, Inc., awarded $300,000 to support research harnessing natural killer (NK) cells for use in immunotherapies. NK cells play a major role in the elimination of both tumors and infected cells, and this research will provide valuable insight that will inform better treatment strategies. A Celebration for the Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber Supporters gathered to celebrate the recently established Fellowship Program in Hematology/Oncology Chair at Dana-Farber. The endowed Chair was funded by colleagues, mentees, grateful patients, family, and friends in honor of Robert J. Mayer, MD, who served as director of the Fellowship Program for more than 35 years. Ann LaCasce, MD, MMSc, who succeeded Mayer as director, was appointed the first incumbent. Pictured (from left): Mayer, LaCasce, and Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD. Richard and Eileen Greisch Richard and Eileen Greisch made a gift of $100,000 to provide essential resources for melanoma research under the direction of Tamara Sussman, MD. These funds will enable researchers to test novel therapeutics in clinical trials, lead investigations in genomic sequencing, and develop groundbreaking immunotherapeutic approaches. Holiday Patient Assistance The Holiday Patient Assistance Program, which helps patients and families in critical financial need, raised $192,785 in 2022. The program helped 726 eligible Dana-Farber patients and families celebrate the season by providing gift cards to help cover the cost of expenses like gas to travel to appointments, groceries for holiday meals, and small gifts for loved ones. Jog for Julie The 7th annual Jog for Julie fundraiser, held in honor of a breast cancer patient, raised more than $30,000 in 2022. The 5K was started in 2014 by Julie’s entire family, including her four children, and has raised more than $220,000 for breast cancer research at Dana-Farber. Michele and Howard Kessler Institute Trustee Michele Kessler and her husband, Howard Kessler, made a gift of $250,000 to launch the Cannabis Care Support Program at Dana-Farber, which aims to create sustainable oncologic cannabis educational resources and advance research on the use of cannabis to address the mental and physical side effects of cancer. Lymphoma Research Foundation As part of their mission to fund innovative research at top institutions around the country, the Lymphoma Research Foundation’s recent funding cycle included awarding grants totaling $115,000 to fund two Dana-Farber studies into advanced treatment options for patients diagnosed with T-cell lymphoma and mantle cell lymphoma. Max Vincze Foundation With a $100,000 grant, the Max Vincze Foundation established a fund to support research into NUT carcinoma, a rare cancer, in honor of Max Vincze, who passed away from the disease in 2021 at the age of 23. National Palliative Care Research Center The National Palliative Care Research Center awarded $198,000 to support the creation of a program to develop nurse-led psychosocial intervention for historically marginalized pediatric patients, with the goal of improving family-centered communication and pediatric patients’ quality of life during treatment. Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor Karen O’Connor and Bruce MacGregor renewed their support for the O’Connor-MacGregor Fund for Melanoma Research with a new $150,000 commitment. This latest gift will support research into the underlying drivers of melanoma and development of durable therapeutic options under the direction of Rizwan Haq, MD, PhD. Poorvu Jaffe Chair Celebration James Tulsky, MD, was named the first incumbent of the Poorvu Jaffe Chair in Psychosocial Oncology and Palliative Care at Dana-Farber, the first chair in this field established at the Institute. The Poorvu Jaffe Family’s gift also established the Poorvu Jaffe Fund for Supportive Oncology and Health Equity. Pictured at a celebration in November 2022 are (standing, from left) Dana-Farber President and CEO Laurie H. Glimcher, MD; Institute Trustee Alison Poorvu Jaffe and Daniel Jaffe; and Tulsky; (seated) Lia and Bill Poorvu. Quest 2 Defy Cancer Over 30 streamers and content creators from around the U.S. participated in the latest Quest 2 Defy Cancer. The program, part of the Jimmy Fund Let's Game® initiative, invites streamers, gamers, and content creators to make an impact on the lifesaving work happening at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute. Swim Across America For 27 years, Swim Across America has supported Dana-Farber through events like their annual Boston Open Water Swim event. In 2022, swimmers of all ages and skill levels raised $142,000 to help support cancer research and care at the Institute, for a lifetime total of more than $3 million. Ware Estate James W. Ware left a generous gift of $334,745 to provide unrestricted support for research and care at Dana-Farber. Unrestricted gifts provide flexible support for programs throughout Dana-Farber, from innovative basic research, to clinical trials, to programs that enhance the Institute’s signature Total Patient Care. William Raveis Ride + Walk The annual William Raveis Ride + Walk raised $115,000 for Dana-Farber in 2022. This event is the largest fundraiser put on by employees from William Raveis Real Estate across New England, New York, and Florida. Load More Briefs

content.text: Stories Archive Image Recognition A new era in cancer care: Lavine Bekenstein Cancer Hospital at Dana-Farber The Lavine Bekenstein Cancer Hospital at Dana-Farber will be the only independent cancer hospital in the region. Image Access and Equity Recognition Total Patient Care More than a building name The historic joint commitment from Anita and Josh Bekenstein and the Jeannie and Jonathan Lavine Family, the largest single gift in Dana-Farber’s history, will help advance a new hospital designed entirely around the needs of cancer patients and their families. Image Basic Science Cancer Research Total Patient Care Yawkey Foundation bridging generations of cancer research and care The Jean and Tom Yawkey Bridge will stand as a special testament to a partnership that has helped carry Dana-Farber from one era of cancer care to the next. Image Basic Science Cancer Research Recognition Total Patient Care From education to excellence: Lubin Family gift supports future of cancer care Richard Lubin has been deeply involved with Dana-Farber Cancer Institute for more than three decades. Image Basic Science Cancer Research Recognition Total Patient Care Honoring a foundation of leadership The specialty floor that will bear the names of past presidents, David G. Nathan, MD, Edward J. Benz Jr., MD, and Laurie H. Glimcher, MD, PhD, in the Lavine Bekenstein Cancer Hospital will one day be a place of highly specialized cancer care. Image Basic Science Cancer Research Recognition Total Patient Care A legacy of giving that makes compassionate care possible The Rosenberg family has long supported cancer patient treatment and care across Boston, a commitment rooted in the values of Leon V. and Marilyn L. Rosenberg and carried forward through generations. Image Cancer Research Recognition Total Patient Care Building a visionary healing environment Since joining the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute Board of Trustees in 2014, Phill Gross has supported Dana-Farber's rapid growth and progress toward a world free from the burden of cancer. Image Recognition Total Patient Care Building the future, one ride at a time Andrew “AJ” Janower and Cindy Janower recently committed $2.5 million through the Pan-Mass Challenge (PMC) to support construction of the facility. Image Basic Science Cancer Research The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research targets hard-to-treat diseases The Mark Foundation for Cancer Research has recently awarded $4.1 million in grants to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute scientists targeting pancreatic cancer, acute myeloid leukemia, and pediatric brain tumors. Image Basic Science Cancer Research Blood Cancer United grants foster research equity, target deadly blood cancers Five Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators are the recipients of $4.2 million in grants from Blood Cancer United to support their innovative work in blood cancer research. Image Basic Science Cancer Research Myeloma Solutions Fund targets multiple myeloma A high-risk form of multiple myeloma (MM) known as t(4;14) is the focus of $2.2 million in research grants from the Myeloma Solutions Fund to two Dana-Farber Cancer Institute investigators. Image Cancer Research Susan G. Komen invests in breakthrough breast cancer research Since its inception in 1982, Susan G. Komen has invested nearly $1.1 billion to accelerate progress and drive innovation in breast cancer research.
